p.src: Now Wang Qing and Duan Sanniang had fought Liao Li for no more than six or seven bouts when Wang Qing spotted an opening and felled him with a thrust of his broad-bladed sword; Duan Sanniang rushed forward and finished him off with another stroke. Liao Li had lived half his life as an outlaw, only for it all to end here like a springtime dream! Raising his broad-bladed sword, Wang Qing shouted, “If any man refuses to submit, let Liao Li be his example!” Seeing Liao Li slain, which of the lackeys dared resist? They all cast down their weapons, bowed, and submitted. Wang Qing led the men up the mountain and reached the stronghold just as the eastern sky was turning pale. On every side of that mountain stood natural stone chambers resembling houses; hence it was called Mount Fang, and it lay under the jurisdiction of Fangzhou. That day Wang Qing settled everyone and their families, counted the lackeys, inventoried the grain, fodder, gold, silver, jewels, brocades, cloth, and other stores in the stronghold, slaughtered oxen and horses, richly rewarded his men, and laid on wine for all to celebrate. The men then acclaimed Wang Qing as master of the stronghold. They forged weapons while drilling the lackeys, preparing to meet the government troops; but no more of that.

p.src: Now the constables, militia, and attendants whom Fangzhou had dispatched that night to arrest Wang Qing were scattered by Wang Qing and his companions. Those who escaped and fled back reported to Prefect Zhang Guxing: “Wang Qing and his men learned of our approach beforehand and resisted the government troops. The chief constable and the informer Huang Da were both killed; those murderous villains have fled westward.” Zhang Guxing was greatly alarmed. The next morning a count showed that more than thirty militiamen had been killed and over forty wounded. That very day Zhang Guxing conferred with the garrison officers of the prefecture and dispatched additional constabulary and garrison troops in pursuit. But the outlaws were so ferocious that the government forces suffered further losses. The ranks of the Mount Fang stronghold swelled daily, and Wang Qing and his men came down from the mountain to plunder households. Seeing the bandits grow rampant, Zhang Guxing issued orders to the subordinate counties, directing them to guard their territories and send troops to join in the suppression; on the other, he again conferred on their suppression with Hu Youwei, the military commissioner commanding Fangzhou’s defense forces. Hu Youwei mustered the garrison troops and chose a day to march against the bandits. Suddenly the troops in both camps raised an uproar: they had received neither pay nor grain for two months, and with empty bellies that day, how could they go and fight bandits? Hearing of the mutiny, Zhang Guxing had no choice but first to distribute one month’s pay and grain. Yet this very distribution only enraged the soldiers further. Why was this? In ordinary times those in authority had neither cared for nor properly disciplined the soldiers; only after the troops had rioted did they issue their due allowances, by which time the soldiers’ insolence had already been indulged. More laughable still, even amid the present emergency, the customary deductions were extorted as ruthlessly as ever. Having so long endured such extortion, the men now vented all their pent-up resentment at once. The army seethed with fury and suddenly erupted, killing Hu Youwei. Seeing that matters had taken a dangerous turn, Zhang Guxing merely secured the official seals and slipped away in advance. With no authority left in the city, local ruffians joined the mutinous soldiers and began burning and plundering the homes of peaceful citizens. When the ruthless bandit Wang Qing saw disorder arise within the city, he seized the opportunity and led his numerous lackeys in an attack on Fangzhou. The mutinous troops and motley rabble of scoundrels in turn submitted to the outlaw. Thus Wang Qing gained the upper hand, and the scoundrel occupied Fangzhou as his lair. In the end Zhang Guxing could not remain hidden and was killed as well.

p.src: Wang Qing seized the money and grain in Fangzhou’s granaries and treasuries, then sent Li Zhu, Duan Er, and Duan Wu separately to the Mount Fang stronghold and other places to raise recruiting banners, buy horses, enlist soldiers, gather fodder, and stockpile grain; villages and towns far and near were all plundered. Idlers, ruffians, rebels, and criminals flocked to join him. At that time Gong Duan and Gong Zheng, whose property had been utterly lost after Huang Da denounced them, heard that Wang Qing was recruiting and came to join the band as well. The neighboring prefectures and counties could do no more than defend their own walls; who dared send troops to suppress him? Within two months the outlaws had gathered more than twenty thousand men and captured the three neighboring walled cities of Shangjin, Zhushan, and Yunxiang counties. The neighboring prefectures and counties reported the matter to the court, which ordered troops in that region to suppress the bandits. The Song government forces often lacked provisions and pay, had fallen out of training, showed no fear of their commanders, while the commanders knew nothing of their troops. At the first alarm of bandits, they loudly proclaimed the enemy fearsome beyond measure, chilling their own soldiers’ hearts and terrifying the people; but when they actually faced the enemy in battle, their generals were cowardly and their soldiers weak and dispirited. How could they withstand Wang Qing’s hordes, who charged in ready to stake their lives? The government troops were routed wherever they met them. Thus Wang Qing’s power grew ever greater, and he went on to capture Nanfeng Prefecture. Later, the officers and troops transferred from the Eastern Capital had obtained their posts either by bribing Cai Jing and Tong Guan or by paying off Yang Jian and Gao Qiu; once those men had received their bribes, what did they care how incompetent or cowardly the appointees were? Having spent heavily to secure their posts and gained authority, those officers wantonly embezzled military provisions, murdered innocent people and claimed merit for it, allowed their troops to plunder, and ravaged the countryside, thereby driving the common people into joining the bandits instead. From then on the bandits steadily gained strength and sent their forces southward. Li Zhu offered a stratagem. Being a native of Jingnan, he disguised himself once more as a physiognomist and astrologer, entered the city, secretly rallied vicious young ruffians and treacherous thugs, and coordinated an attack from within and without that took the city of Jingnan. Wang Qing then appointed Li Zhu as his military adviser and proclaimed himself “King of Chu.” Thereupon great river-and-sea bandits and outlaws from mountain strongholds all came to join him. Within three or four years he occupied six military prefectures of the Song realm. Wang Qing then built grand audience halls, inner gardens, and palaces within Nanfeng, usurped royal titles, and proclaimed a new era name; in imitation of the Song court, he established a spurious bureaucracy of civil and military offices, ministries and councils, palace ministers and field commanders. He appointed Li Zhu military adviser and chief chancellor; Fang Han commissioner of military affairs; Duan Er grand general commanding the forces that protected the realm; Duan Wu chief commander of the forces that supported the realm; Fan Quan commander of the palace guard; Gong Duan pacification commissioner; Gong Zheng transport commissioner, with sole charge of receipts and disbursements and the accounting of money and grain; and Qiu Xiang commander of the imperial camp; and he falsely installed Lady Duan as his consort. From the time he began his rebellion in the first year of Xuanhe until the spring of its fifth year—when Song Jiang and his men were campaigning against Tian Hu in Hebei and confronting him at Huguan—Wang Qing over in Huaixi captured Yunan Commandery and Wanzhou as well, bringing the total number of military prefectures under his occupation to eight. Those eight were Nanfeng, Jingnan, Shannan, Yunan, Ande, Dongchuan, Wanzhou, and Xijing. Together, the prefectures and counties subordinate to those eight regions numbered eighty-six. Wang Qing also built a temporary palace at Yunan and appointed Shi Jun as resident governor to defend Yunan Commandery.

p.src: At first, when Wang Qing ordered Liu Min and the others to seize Wanzhou, the prefecture lay close to the Eastern Capital, so Cai Jing and his fellows could not conceal the matter from the emperor. They reported it to Emperor Daojun, who commanded Cai You and Tong Guan to campaign against Wang Qing and relieve Wanzhou. But Cai You and Tong Guan kept no discipline in their army and treated their soldiers brutally, so morale collapsed. Liu Min and the others inflicted a crushing defeat upon them, and Wanzhou consequently fell, throwing the Eastern Capital into terror. Fearing punishment, Cai You and Tong Guan concealed the truth from the emperor alone. After defeating Cai You and Tong Guan, the rebel commanders Liu Min, Lu Cheng, and the others proceeded to lay siege to Luzhou and Xiangzhou. Fortunately, Song Jiang and his men returned after pacifying Hebei and once again received an imperial command, this time to campaign against Huaixi. Truly, they had no time even to warm their seats, nor could their horses halt their hooves! Commanding a great army of more than two hundred thousand, they set out southward. They had barely crossed the Yellow River when the central authorities sent another urgent dispatch, pressing Pacification Commissioner Chen and Song Jiang to hasten with their forces to the relief of Luzhou and Xiangzhou. Braving the summer heat, Song Jiang and his men drove their sweating horses onward, coming by way of Suxian and Sishui; wherever they passed, they did not harm so much as a hair. The great army had already reached the borders of Yangdi Prefecture; when the rebels heard that Song Jiang's army was approaching, they lifted both sieges, at Luzhou and Xiangzhou, and withdrew.

p.src: At that time, Zhang Qing, Qiongying, and Ye Qing had witnessed Tian Hu's execution, received imperial favor, and been ordered to assist Song Jiang in the campaign against Wang Qing. Zhang Qing and the others had left the Eastern Capital and had already been in Yingchang Prefecture for more than half a month. On hearing that Vanguard Song's army had arrived, the three went before the army to welcome him. After paying their respects, they related in full how they had received imperial commendation and titles. Song Jiang and all his officers praised them without end. Song Jiang ordered Zhang Qing and the others to remain with the army and await assignment.

p.src: Song Jiang asked Pacification Commissioner Chen, Staff Adviser Hou, Luo Wuyu, and the others to station themselves within the city of Yangdi, as it was inconvenient for his own great army to enter the city. Song Jiang then gave orders for the whole army to encamp in the deep, densely shaded woods of Mount Fangcheng to escape the summer heat. Moreover, because the soldiers had marched a thousand li and many were exhausted or stricken by heat, he ordered An Daoquan to prepare medicines and treat them; he also had the soldiers erect cool shelters and settle the horses there, ordering Huangfu Duan to tend them and promptly shear their manes. Wu Yong said, “With the great army encamped amid dense woods, I fear the enemy may use fire.” Song Jiang replied, “That is precisely what I want them to do.” Song Jiang then ordered the soldiers to build a small projecting shed of bamboo matting and thatch beneath the cool shade trees on a high ridge of that mountain. Qiao Daoqing, one of the surrendered commanders from Hebei, understood his intent and came to report to Song Jiang: “I, Qiao, am deeply grateful for the vanguard's generous favor. Today I wish to render some small service.” Song Jiang was delighted. He secretly imparted his plan to Qiao Daoqing, who then went to the mountain shed. Song Jiang selected thirty thousand strong and able soldiers. He ordered Zhang Qing and Qiongying to command ten thousand troops and lie in ambush at the eastern foot of the mountain; and ordered Sun An and Bian Xiang likewise to command ten thousand troops and lie in ambush at the western foot. “As soon as you hear the thunder cannon sound from my central army, charge out together.” He had all the grain and fodder piled on the level ground at the southern foot of the mountain and ordered Li Ying and Chai Jin to guard it with five thousand soldiers.

p.src: The assignments had scarcely been completed when Gongsun Sheng said, “Elder Brother, your plan is most ingenious! Yet in this stifling heat, the soldiers have been worn down by marching and sickness. If the enemy's elite troops should suddenly attack, then even though our forces outnumber theirs ten to one, we will surely be unable to prevail. Allow this humble Daoist to perform a trifling art, first dispelling everyone's vexation. Once men and horses are cool and refreshed, they will naturally regain their strength.” When he had finished speaking, he took up his sword and performed the rite. His feet traced the two characters of the Dipper and Northern Ladle; his left hand formed the thunder seal and his right the sword sign. Concentrating his spirit in visualization, he drew a breath of vital air from the southeast and recited an incantation. In a moment, cool winds whispered and dark clouds drifted forth, welling from the peaks and caverns of the mountain until they enveloped all Mount Fangcheng. More than two hundred thousand men and horses were bathed in cool winds and refreshing air. Everywhere beyond that mountain, however, the blazing sun still seemed hot enough to melt gold and iron; cicadas shrilled in confusion, while birds hid themselves away. Song Jiang and all the others were overjoyed and thanked Gongsun Sheng, praising his divine powers and virtue. After six or seven days of this, with An Daoquan treating the men and Huangfu Duan tending the horses, soldiers and mounts gradually recovered their vigor; but no more need be said of that.

p.src: At that moment, Vanguard Song ordered Ling Zhen to fire the signal cannon, and its report soared high into the sky and thundered. From the east came Zhang Qing and Qiongying, and from the west Sun An and Bian Xiang, each leading troops in a furious charge. The rebel army suffered a crushing defeat: Sun An cut Lu Cheng in two with a single stroke of his sword; Qiongying knocked Zheng Jie from his horse with a stone, and Zhang Qing finished him off with a thrust of his spear; Bian Xiang speared Gu Cen to death; Kou Meng was killed amid the melee; Of the twenty-three thousand men and horses, more than half were lost to fire and weapons, while the rest fled in all directions; all two thousand carts were burned to ashes; Only Liu Min, with three or four hundred battered survivors, escaped ahead and fled to Wanzhou. The Song army had not burned so much as half a stalk of fodder, nor lost a single soldier, and captured great numbers of horses, suits of armor, gongs, and drums. Zhang Qing, Sun An, and the others returned victorious to the mountain stronghold to report their achievements. Sun An presented Lu Cheng's head; Zhang Qing and Qiongying presented Zheng Jie's head; and Bian Xiang presented Gu Cen's head. Song Jiang rewarded each of them, recording Qiao Daoqing as first in merit, followed in order by Zhang Qing, Qiongying, Sun An, and Bian Xiang.

p.src: Wu Yong said, “Elder Brother's ingenious stratagem has already broken the rebels' nerve. But Wanzhou is encircled by winding hills and streams, its uplands and plains are rich and fertile, and the region is famed as a land of abundance. If the rebels redeploy their commanders and defend it with a great force, it will be difficult to take quickly. Now the autumn wind has driven off the heat, and the jeweled dew brings coolness; our men and horses have all recovered their strength. We must take advantage of our army's soaring morale and the weakness of the garrison to attack swiftly, and the city will surely fall. But we must also divide off forces to encamp north and south, so as to block any rebel relief troops that may charge upon us.” Song Jiang approved and issued orders according to the plan. Guan Sheng, Qin Ming, Yang Zhi, Huang Xin, Sun Li, Xuan Zan, Hao Siwen, Chen Da, Yang Chun, and Zhou Tong were to command thirty thousand troops and encamp east of Wanzhou to guard against rebel reinforcements coming from the south; Lin Chong, Huyan Zhuo, Dong Ping, Suo Chao, Han Tao, Peng Qi, Shan Tinggui, Wei Dingguo, Ou Peng, and Deng Fei were to lead thirty thousand troops and encamp west of Wanzhou to resist rebel forces coming from the north. The commanders obeyed, mustered their troops and horses, and departed. Then Sun An and the other sixteen surrendered commanders from Hebei came forward together and reported, “We have been accepted into the Vanguard's service and are deeply grateful for the honor and courtesy he has shown us. Now we wish to serve as the vanguard and go ahead to attack the city, that we may repay some small part of this great kindness.” Song Jiang consented and ordered Zhang Qing and Qiongying to command Sun An and the other seventeen officers, together with fifty thousand troops, as the advance force. The seventeen were Sun An, Ma Ling, Bian Xiang, Shan Shiqi, Tang Bin, Wen Zhongrong, Cui Ye, Jin Ding, Huang Yue, Mei Yu, Jin Zhen, Bi Sheng, Pan Xun, Yang Fang, Feng Sheng, Hu Bi, and Ye Qing. Zhang Qing at once obeyed the order and led the officers and troops on their advance toward Wanzhou.

p.src: Song Jiang, together with Lu Junyi, Wu Yong, and the others, commanded the remaining officers and main army, struck camp, left Mount Fangcheng, and marched south, pitching camp ten li outside Wanzhou. He ordered Li Yun, Tang Long, and Tao Zongwang to supervise the construction of siege engines and send them forward for Zhang Qing and the others to use. Zhang Qing and the other commanders led their troops in surrounding Wanzhou so tightly that not even water could have escaped. The city's defending commander, Liu Min, was the man who had fallen into Song Jiang's trap that night and barely escaped with his life. As soon as he reached Wanzhou, he sent a messenger to report to Wang Qing in the south and dispatched documents to neighboring prefectures and counties requesting reinforcements. Now that the Song troops had surrounded the city, he ordered his men simply to hold it fast and wait for reinforcements before launching a counterattack. The Song troops attacked the city for six or seven days in succession, but the walls were strong and could not be taken quickly. North of Wanzhou, adjoining Ruzhou, the rebel commander Zhang Shou came with twenty thousand relief troops. Lin Chong and the others killed their commander Zhang Shou, and all the remaining lesser officers and soldiers scattered in rout. That same day, relief troops also arrived from Anchang, Yiyang, and other counties south of Wanzhou. Guan Sheng and the others routed them, captured their commanders Bai Ren and Zhang Yi, and sent them to Song Jiang's main camp, where they were duly executed. A great many enemies were slain or captured in the two engagements. By then, Li Yun and the others had completed the siege engines. Sun An, Ma Ling, and the others worked with one accord, ordering the soldiers to fill sacks with earth and heap them up on all four sides, drawing ever closer to the city walls; They also chose brave and nimble men, who used flying bridges and wheeled siege engines to cross the trenches and moats. The soldiers all fought courageously to scale the walls, and thus Wanzhou was taken. The defending commander Liu Min was captured alive; more than twenty lesser officers were killed, over five thousand soldiers were slain, and ten thousand surrendered. Song Jiang and the main army entered the city, executed Liu Min and displayed his head, then posted proclamations to reassure the people. The merits of Guan Sheng, Lin Chong, Zhang Qing, Sun An, and the other commanders were recorded in order. Messengers were sent to Pacification Commissioner Chen at Yangzhai Prefecture to report the victory and request that he and his staff transfer their headquarters to Wanzhou. Pacification Commissioner Chen was overjoyed by the news and immediately came to Wanzhou with Staff Officer Hou and Military Instructor Luo. Song Jiang and the others went outside the city to welcome them and escorted them within. It need hardly be said that Pacification Commissioner Chen praised Song Jiang and the others for their distinguished service.

p.src: Song Jiang attended to military affairs in Wanzhou for more than ten days. It was now early in the eighth month, and the summer heat was gradually receding. Song Jiang consulted Wu Yong, saying, “Which city should we take next?” Wu Yong replied, “South of here lies the Shannan Command. To the south it reaches the regions of Hunan and Hubei, while to the north it commands the passes and Luoyang; it stands at the vital junction between Chu and Shu. We should take that city first, thereby dividing the rebels' strength.” Song Jiang said, “The Military Advisor's words accord perfectly with my own thoughts.” He therefore left Hua Rong, Lin Chong, Xuan Zan, Hao Siwen, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng to assist Pacification Commissioner Chen and his staff, commanding fifty thousand troops to garrison Wanzhou. Pacification Commissioner Chen also retained Xiao Rang, the “Master Calligrapher,” and sent orders to the eight naval commanders, including Li Jun, to command the fleet up the Bi River and rendezvous on the Han River north of Shannan city.
